_comment: Change set 4 (evidence linkage) — Step 0 findings and predictions, committed before any linker code was written. Run under the user's instruction to proceed through every stop-gate; every value is PROVISIONAL — not ratified. A mismatch is reported, never adjusted away.

step0.stage4Today: Same-sentence proximity only. extractClaims.detectCitations finds tokens in the claim's own sentence (doi, url, numeric [n], author-year, (year), attribution phrases such as 'according to' / 'source:' / 'data from'); analyze.markOwnSiteUrls turns publisher-host URLs into url-own; gradeEvidence walks the rubric ladder top-down by those token types and the claim's keywords, with an own-result claim lifted to rubric.ownResultRung. Nothing links a claim to a reference entry, a footnote, a caption or a section; segment.js sets the reference list aside 'No linking'.
step0.captionsInIngestion: Not labeled. extractPdf.js segregates small-font text (captions/credits) to the end of each page but marks nothing; nonClaimFilter demotes 'Figure N:' captions. So the linker falls back to lines and inline spans beginning 'Source:' (per the handoff), and to 'Figure/Fig./Exhibit/Chart/Table N' references.

fixtures.fixture-a-cadre: 105 reference entries after the References heading (author-year, APA-like: 'Araujo, D. M., … (2020). Cognitive …'); 71 author-year anchors in the body, often split by the two-column merge; 0 numbered markers; 0 footnotes; 46 URLs in the body; 0 'Source:' lines; 2 figure references.
fixtures.fixture-b-pew-report: No reference list; 0 author-year anchors in the body except a methods line ('Hur, Achen (2013)'); 0 URLs; 19 inline 'Source: Survey of U.S. workers conducted Oct. 7-13, 2024.' inside chart notes (the chart-note sentences are dropped as non-claims; the claims above them are the chart titles and prose); no footnotes.
fixtures.fixture-c-gensler-fandom-2026: No reference list; 0 markers; 25 URLs (credits and footers); 9 standalone 'Source: Post-World Cup Survey' / 'Source: In-Match Social Media Analysis' lines closing chart blocks, each page opened by a running 'EXECUTIVE SUMMARY' header; no footnotes. The handoff's check claim ('Our pre-World Cup survey data shows that 9 of 10 respondents…', p11) has no Source line in its block, so it can link only by section scope.

decisions: A resolved marker keeps its own token type for grading (numeric / author-year); the reference entry it resolves to (and any DOI there) is recorded on the link but does not move the rung. Grading by the quality of the target is a ladder change, left to change set 6.
Same-sentence tokens that the attribution routing does not prefer are kept as 'proximity' links, so no evidence the sentence carries is lost and reliance on proximity is measurable.
An own-study link (caption naming the document's own study, or section scope) lifts the claim to rubric.ownResultRung, as an own-result claim already is.
Section kinds: an Executive Summary, Key Takeaways or Highlights heading, and a short heading naming the document's own survey/analysis ('POST-WORLD CUP SURVEY'), read as key findings.
An unlinked claim records evidence.status 'unlinked' with the bases tried; its rung stays the ladder's floor (the ladder and its labels are out of scope).

linksPerBasis._basis: Counts of links on extracted claims. Ranges set from the Step 0 inventory above.

markersResolved._basis: share of author-year anchors that match an entry by first author and year; the two-column merge splits some names

flagCounts._basis: Only own-study links (captions, section scope) and footnotes can lift a rung; A has neither (narrative review, no captions). causal-overreach reads the design, not the rung, so it does not move.

predictions.fixtureCCheckClaim: links to the report's own survey by section scope (no caption in its block)
predictions.knownGoodString: flags unchanged (no own study, no captions; its citations are same-sentence)
